schema.description: GetTemplateResponse is the response for getting a template.

convertedHooks.description:
Read-only, legacy templates only: the hooks the fixed mapping derives
from warmup_script and startup_script — exactly what a session created
from this template runs in a workspace with lifecycle hooks enabled, and
what the editor starts from when the template is converted to hooks.
Unset on a hooks template. Ignored on writes.

onClaim.description: On claim script. Unset means the template has no On claim hook.

onCreate.description: On create script. Unset means the template has no On create hook.

onRestore.description: On restore script. Unset means the template has no On restore hook.

createdByEmail.description: Email of the user who created this template (owner).

description.description: Description explaining what this template is for.

deviceSpec.description:
The virtual device every session created from this template boots — the
same message CreateSessionRequest.device_spec and preview links carry.
Unset = no device. A session request may replace it, tweak it field by
field (see CreateSessionRequest.device_spec) or skip it (no_device).

coldBoot.description:
Android only: boot the emulator cold (-no-snapshot-load) and never save a
quickboot snapshot, so every open exercises a full first boot.

cores.description:
Android only: emulator CPU core count. 0 = sized to the host (cores/2,
clamped). Same mint bound + on-VM clamp as ram_mb.

deviceModel.description: Device profile hint (for example, "pixel_7"). Empty = platform default.

osVersion.description:
iOS only: the simulator runtime to boot, as an iOS version such as "18.2"
(or a simctl runtime id). Anything else, and any value on Android, is
rejected. Empty = the newest installed runtime. Reads back as the version.

platform.description:
Device platform: "android" (emulator, Linux stacks) or "ios" (simulator,
macOS stacks).

ramMb.description:
Android only: emulator RAM in MB. 0 = sized to the host (RAM/4, clamped).
Bounded at mint against the machine type's specs; clamped again on the VM
with a degradation notice if the host cannot honor it.

systemImage.description:
Android only: sdkmanager system image package (for example,
"system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64"). Empty = platform
default. Images not pre-installed on the stack fall back to the best
installed one with a viewer-visible degradation notice — they are never
downloaded at boot.

featureFlags.description: Feature flags available for this template.

items.description: FeatureFlag represents a toggleable feature for a template.

description.description: Description explaining what this feature flag enables.

hooks.description: The lifecycle hooks of a "hooks" template; unset on a legacy template.

onClaim.description: On claim script. Unset means the template has no On claim hook.

onCreate.description: On create script. Unset means the template has no On create hook.

onRestore.description: On restore script. Unset means the template has no On restore hook.

image.description:
Machine image name (for example, "osx-xcode-edge"). Consistent across clusters.

Superseded by stack_id (prefer it). The image is a merged-stack id that
bundles many Xcode versions; stack_id is the stable, specific contract.

lifecycleMode.description:
How the template's scripts are stored and run (lifecycle hooks,
docs/lifecycle-hooks/DESIGN.md). "legacy": warmup_script and
startup_script, run by the instance manager's two stages as before.
"hooks": the lifecycle hooks in `hooks`, run on the booted VM by the RDE
runner. In a workspace with lifecycle hooks enabled a legacy template
runs through a fixed mapping applied when a session is created (On
create = the warmup part, then the startup part in the background; On
restore = the startup part in the background); it becomes a hooks
template only when it is saved with `hooks`.

machineType.description: Machine type name (for example, "g2.mac.m2pro.4c"). Consistent across clusters.

servicePorts.description: Network services this template's sessions expose (rendered as SSH tunnel help).

items.description:
ServicePort represents a network service a template's sessions expose on the VM
(for example a dev web server). Sessions snapshot these and the UI renders
SSH tunnel (ssh -L) connection help from them.

description.description: Description shown next to the tunnel help (for example, "Storybook dev server").

localPort.description:
Suggested local port for the tunnel. 0 means "same as port". Use when the
remote port commonly clashes with something on developer machines.

name.description: Short name of the service (for example, "web-app"). Unique per template.

port.description: Port the service listens on inside the VM (1-65535).

sessionInputs.description: Session inputs that users must or may provide when creating a session.

items.description:
SessionInput defines an input that users must or may provide when creating a session.
Configured by the template author. Filled by the session starter.

defaultValue.description:
Default value used in boot scripts when the session starter leaves the field blank.
Only applicable when required is false.

description.description: Description explaining what this input is for.

exposeAsEnvVar.description: Whether to expose this input as an ENV VAR in interactive terminal sessions.

hook.description:
The scope that receives this input (docs/lifecycle-hooks/DESIGN.md
§13): "shared" (the default when empty) reaches every hook and is
supplied when the session or the pool is created; "on_create" is
supplied with the pool (or the direct create) and reaches On create
only; "on_claim" and "on_restore" are supplied by whoever claims (or
at a direct create) and reach that hook only. Keys are unique per
scope; the same key may exist on several scopes.

key.description: Key/name of the input (matches saved_inputs.key for auto-prefill).

required.description: Whether this input is required. If false, the input is optional and default_value is used when not provided.

stackId.description:
Stack id (for example, "osx-xcode-16.0.x-edge"). The stable contract stored on the
template; resolved to a provisionable image at session-start time.

startupScript.description: Startup script (bash) that runs every time the session starts or restarts.

templateVariables.description: Template variables baked into this template (available in boot scripts).

items.description:
TemplateVariable represents a baked-in variable for a template.
Available in boot scripts. Optionally exposed as an ENV VAR in terminal sessions.

exposeAsEnvVar.description:
Whether to also write this value to the session's shell profile when
its scope's step runs ("Also in terminal"), so it is available in SSH
and terminal sessions afterwards. Refused on a protected variable.

hook.description:
The scope that receives this variable (docs/lifecycle-hooks/DESIGN.md
§13): "shared" (the default when empty) reaches every hook; "on_create",
"on_claim" or "on_restore" reach that hook only. Per-hook scopes exist
only on a template with lifecycle hooks. Keys are unique per scope; the
hook's own value wins over a shared value of the same key.

isSecret.description: Whether this is a secret value.

protected.description:
Write-only: never returned by the API, replaced but never viewed.
Implies is_secret. For secrets every pool of the template reuses.

value.description:
Value of the variable. For secret variables this is empty unless the request
explicitly set include_secrets=true (see GetTemplateRequest/ListTemplatesRequest).

updatedAt.description: When the template was last updated.

warmupScript.description:
Warmup script (bash) that runs only once during initial session creation.
Use for setup tasks like dependency installation.

workingDirectory.description:
Working directory for terminal sessions. If set, terminals start in this directory
instead of the home directory. Must be an absolute path.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID that this template is associated with.

workspaceLinks.description: Workspace links configured for this template.

items.description: WorkspaceLink represents a configured IDE workspace folder link for a template.

featureFlagId.description: Optional feature flag ID that controls visibility.

folderPath.description: Remote folder path to open (for example, "/Users/vagrant/ios-app").

label.description: Display label for the button (for example, "iOS App").
